mainTopic: Shared and partial killing (גוסס, טריפה), רבא's rulings about a טריפה, the snake-bite case, and a victim who improved before dying
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier answer: a thrower's force is 'weak,' but it still counts as his. A ברייתא then teaches that if ten people beat a man to death, all are פטור, while רבי יהודה בן בתירא makes the last attacker חייב when the blows came one after another. רבי יוחנן shows that both sides read ״כל נפש״ differently. רבא narrows the argument: everyone agrees that killing a טריפה is פטור and that killing a גוסס בידי שמים is חייב, so they argue only about a גוסס בידי אדם. A ברייתא recited before רב ששת is corrected and shown to follow רבי יהודה בן בתירא. Next comes a series of rulings by רבא about a טריפה: as a murderer, as a sinner with a male, as a witness, and as the owner of an ox. Several of them rest on the rule that testimony which can never face הזמה is not testimony, and רב אשי disagrees on two of them. The גמרא then explains the snake case in the משנה: it depends on whether the venom sits ready in the snake's teeth or the snake releases it itself. Finally a new משנה asks about a victim who improved and then died, and the גמרא starts bringing רבי נחמיה's פסוק, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: His force is weak, but it is still his force
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes an answer from the earlier discussion. The stone's sideways movement still comes from the thrower's force, even though that force is weak.
steps.simpleTranslation: If it were not his force, the stone would just fall straight down. So it really is his force, only a weak force.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing an answer from before this section. It shows that the stone's path still comes from the thrower, even though his push is weak.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A stone with nothing pushing it would just fall straight down. Since it moved some other way, something is still pushing it, and that push comes from the thrower. So the force is called 'weak' (כח כחוש), but it is still counted as his.

keyTerms.meaning: His force: the power that comes from the person's own action
A weak force: weakened, but still the person's force

phrases.english: And if it were not his force,
phrases.notes: This points back to the case just before: a stone that was thrown, not one that just dropped straight down.

phrases.english: it should go straight down.
Rather, it is a weak force.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָאו כֹּחוֹ הוּא תֵּיזִיל לְתַחַת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer from the discussion before this section.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefines the force: it is weak, but it is still attributed to the person.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: One might think the stone's movement is no longer the thrower's doing.
steps.terutzMaskana: Without his force the stone would simply drop, so its path still comes from him, as a weak force.

steps.title: Ten people hit a man with ten sticks: the first view
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that if ten people beat a man with ten sticks and he dies, all of them are פטור. This is true whether they hit him at the same time or one after another.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: If ten people hit a man with ten sticks and he died, they are all exempt. This is true whether they hit him at the same moment or one after the other.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic with a ברייתא. Its first opinion says that when many people together cause a death, none of them gets the death penalty for murder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: No single attacker killed the man by himself, so no one is liable. The ברייתא stresses that even one-after-another is פטור. That sets up the next opinion, which disagrees about exactly that case.
steps.confusionAlert: פטורין here means they are not executed for murder. It does not mean that what they did was allowed.

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
If ten people struck him
with ten sticks, and he died,
whether at the same moment,
or one after the other, they are exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן הִכּוּהוּ עֲשָׂרָה בְּנֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic: a death caused by several attackers.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ten attackers whose blows together killed a man are all פטור, whether they hit him at the same time or one after another.

steps.title: The last attacker is liable for making death come sooner
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בן בתירא disagrees about the one-after-another case. He holds that the last attacker is liable because he made the man die sooner.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה בן בתירא says: If they hit him one after the other, the last one is liable, because he brought the man's death closer.
steps.whatsHappening: A second opinion in the same ברייתא disagrees about the case where the blows came one after another.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He agrees that when everyone hits at the same moment, all are פטור. In the one-after-another case, though, the last blow made the death happen sooner. That is enough to make the last attacker a murderer.

keyTerms.meaning: He brought his death closer, made him die sooner

steps.whyThisMatters: This raises a basic question: is someone who only speeds up a death that was already coming called a killer?

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira says:
If one after the other, the last one is liable,
because he brought his death closer.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first opinion, but only about the one-after-another case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the attackers hit one after another, the last one is חייב because he made the death come sooner.

steps.title: Both sides read the same פסוק differently
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that both opinions come from the words ״כל נפש״. The רבנן read it as 'a whole life.' רבי יהודה בן בתירא reads it as 'any amount of life.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Both of them learned from one פסוק: 'And a man who strikes any soul of a person.' The רבנן hold that 'כל נפש' means he is liable only when he took a whole life. רבי יהודה בן בתירא holds that 'כל נפש' means anything that is a life, even a little.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן shows where each side's opinion comes from. Both read the same words of the תורה, but they understand them differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The argument hangs on the word כל. The רבנן read it as 'whole': you must take a complete life, and the last attacker did not. רבי יהודה בן בתירא reads it as 'any': taking whatever life is left still counts as murder.

keyTerms.meaning: They learned from one and the same פסוק
'Any soul' or 'a whole soul': the key words of the פסוק

steps.whatToRemember: The מחלוקת comes down to ״כל נפש״. 'Whole life' leads to פטור, and 'any bit of life' makes the last attacker חייב.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
And both of them learned from one verse:
"And a man who strikes any soul of a person."
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:17

phrases.english: The Rabbis hold: "any soul" means
not until there is a whole soul,
phrases.notes: In other words, he is liable only if he took the person's whole life by himself.

phrases.aramaic: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בֶּן בְּתִירָא סָבַר: ״כׇּל נֶפֶשׁ״ –
phrases.english: and Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira holds: "any soul" means
anything that is a soul, any amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind both sides of the ברייתא's מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sides learn from ״כל נפש״. The רבנן read it as 'a whole life,' and רבי יהודה בן בתירא reads it as 'any amount of life.'

steps.title: Two cases where everyone agrees
steps.stepSummary: רבא says both sides agree that killing a טריפה is פטור. They also agree that killing a גוסס בידי שמים is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Everyone agrees that someone who kills a טריפה is exempt. Everyone also agrees that someone who kills a person dying by the hand of Heaven is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא begins to narrow down what the מחלוקת is really about. He first gives two cases where both sides agree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טריפה has a fatal wound, and the law treats him almost like a dead person, so killing him is פטור. A גוסס בידי שמים is dying from illness, and no person has harmed him yet, so the killer took his remaining life alone and is חייב. These two cases are the clear ends of the range.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with a fatal wound who is expected to die
A person in the final stage before death
By the hand of Heaven: from illness or natural causes

phrases.english: Rava said:
All agree about one who kills a tereifa
that he is exempt;
and about one who kills a person dying by the hand of Heaven,
phrases.notes: The words 'one who kills' carry over from the first case. The גמרא does not repeat them.

phrases.english: that he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Narrows the מחלוקת by first naming two cases where both sides agree.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Killing a טריפה is פטור, and killing a גוסס בידי שמים is חייב, according to everyone.

steps.title: The argument is only about a person dying from human blows
steps.stepSummary: רבא says the מחלוקת is only about a גוסס בידי אדם. One side compares him to a טריפה, so his killer is פטור. The other side compares him to a גוסס בידי שמים, so his killer is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: They disagree only about a person dying by the hand of a person. One master compares him to a טריפה, and the other master compares him to someone dying by the hand of Heaven.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא names the one case the מחלוקת is really about. He explains each side as a comparison to one of the two cases everyone agrees on.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The man beaten by the first nine attackers is a גוסס בידי אדם. The רבנן compare him to a טריפה, so the last attacker is פטור. רבי יהודה בן בתירא compares him to a גוסס בידי שמים, so the last attacker is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: By the hand of a person: from injuries people caused

steps.whatToRemember: טריפה is פטור and גוסס בידי שמים is חייב according to everyone. The ten-attackers מחלוקת is about a גוסס בידי אדם, and it depends on which of these two cases he is more like.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two kinds of גוסס. Killing a גוסס from illness is חייב according to everyone. Only a גוסס from human blows is argued about.

phrases.english: They disagreed only
about a person dying by the hand of a person.
One master compares him to a tereifa,
phrases.notes: This 'one master' is the רבנן, who exempt the last attacker.

phrases.aramaic: וּמָר מְדַמֵּי לֵיהּ לְגוֹסֵס בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם.
phrases.english: and the other master compares him to one dying by the hand of Heaven.

steps.triggerLanguage: לֹא נֶחְלְקוּ אֶלָּא בְּגוֹסֵס בִּידֵי אָדָם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the two agreed cases from the previous step to place the machlokes.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The ten-attackers מחלוקת is about a גוסס בידי אדם. The רבנן compare him to a טריפה (פטור), and רבי יהודה בן בתירא compares him to a גוסס בידי שמים (חייב).

steps.title: Why not compare him to one dying by Heaven?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the side that compares a גוסס בידי אדם to a טריפה why they don't compare him to a גוסס בידי שמים instead.
steps.simpleTranslation: The one who compares him to a טריפה, why doesn't he compare him to someone dying at the hands of Heaven?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is testing the first side of רבא's explanation. It asks why this side picked the טריפה comparison and not the other one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A גוסס בידי אדם looks a bit like both cases. He is dying, like a גוסס בידי שמים, but he was hurt by a person. The גמרא wants a reason for choosing the טריפה comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: The one who compares him (to another case)
A person with a fatal injury to a vital organ
A person dying from natural causes, such as illness

phrases.english: The one who compares him to a טריפה,
phrases.notes: "Him" is the גוסס בידי אדם from רבא's statement, someone dying because a person hurt him.

phrases.english: what is the reason he does not compare him
to someone dying at the hands of Heaven?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאן דִּמְדַמֵּי לֵיהּ לִטְרֵיפָה, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא מְדַמֵּי לֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind the first side of רבא's explanation in step 6.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the side that says פטור chose the טריפה comparison over the גוסס בידי שמים comparison.

steps.title: A person already acted on him
steps.stepSummary: No person did anything to a גוסס בידי שמים, but someone already attacked this person, so he is more like a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: With someone dying at the hands of Heaven, no action was done to him by a person. This one did have an action done to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for the first side: the key difference is whether a person already acted on the victim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: With a גוסס בידי שמים, the only person who acts is the final killer, so he is fully responsible. With a גוסס בידי אדם, an earlier attacker already acted, so the killing is shared, like the ten attackers in step 2, and the last one is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: An action, here an act of hitting done by a person

phrases.english: Someone dying at the hands of Heaven
no action was done to him,
but this one had an action done to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוֹסֵס בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם לָא אִיתְעֲבִיד בֵּיהּ מַעֲשֶׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A person already acted on the גוסס בידי אדם. A person did not act on the גוסס בידי שמים. So the גוסס בידי אדם is closer to a טריפה.

steps.title: Why not compare him to a טריפה?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the other side why they don't compare a גוסס בידי אדם to a טריפה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the one who compares him to someone dying at the hands of Heaven, why doesn't he compare him to a טריפה?
steps.whatsHappening: Now the גמרא tests the second side, the one that says the killer is חייב, and asks why they reject the טריפה comparison.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This mirrors step 7. The question is especially strong because step 8 just gave a good reason to compare him to a טריפה, since a person already acted on him.

keyTerms.meaning: A person dying because another person hurt him

phrases.aramaic: וּמַאן דִּמְדַמֵּי לֵיהּ לְגוֹסֵס בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם,
phrases.english: And the one who compares him to someone dying at the hands of Heaven,

phrases.aramaic: מַאי טַעְמָא לָא מְדַמֵּי לֵיהּ לִטְרֵיפָה?
phrases.english: what is the reason he does not compare him to a טריפה?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּמַאן דִּמְדַמֵּי לֵיהּ לְגוֹסֵס בִּידֵי שָׁמַיִם, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא מְדַמֵּי לֵיהּ לִטְרֵיפָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from the first side of רבא's explanation to the second side, using the same pattern as step 7.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the side that says חייב chose the גוסס בידי שמים comparison over the טריפה comparison.

steps.title: A טריפה's vital organs are already cut
steps.stepSummary: A טריפה is like someone whose vital organs are already cut. A גוסס בידי אדם does not have that kind of damage.
steps.simpleTranslation: A טריפה is like someone whose סימנים are cut. This one's סימנים are not cut.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the reason for the second side: a טריפה has a specific deadly injury, but this victim does not.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טריפה is treated as if he were already slaughtered, so killing him is not counted as killing. The גוסס בידי אדם is just very weak and dying, which is more like a גוסס בידי שמים, so his killer is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: The windpipe and the food pipe, the organs cut in שחיטה

steps.whatToRemember: Side that says פטור: a person already acted on him, so he is like a טריפה. Side that says חייב: his vital organs are not cut, so he is like a גוסס בידי שמים.

phrases.english: A טריפה is like one whose organs are cut,
phrases.notes: The סימנים are the windpipe and food pipe. Once they are cut, it is as if the person were already slaughtered.

phrases.english: but this one's organs are not cut.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A טריפה is like one whose סימנים are cut, so he counts as already dead. The גוסס בידי אדם has no such damage, so he is like a גוסס בידי שמים.

steps.title: A ברייתא about a second attacker who finishes the killing
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from ״כל נפש אדם״ that if one person hits someone with a blow that cannot kill and another person then kills him, the second person is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: A תנא taught before רב ששת: "And a man who strikes any soul of a person" comes to include one who hits his friend with a blow that cannot kill, and then another person comes and kills him. The second one is חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new source, a ברייתא recited before רב ששת, about two attackers where the second finishes the killing.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the extra word ״כל״ in the פסוק to include a case. As it is worded here, the first blow could not kill, and the second attacker is חייב. The next step will question this wording.

keyTerms.meaning: Liable, here to be killed as a murderer

phrases.english: A tanna taught before Rav Sheshet:
phrases.notes: This תנא is a person in the בית מדרש whose job was to memorize and recite ברייתות.

phrases.english: "And a man who strikes any soul of a person"
phrases.notes: ויקרא 24:17

phrases.english: comes to include one who strikes his fellow
and the blow does not have enough force to kill,
and another comes and kills him,
that he is liable.
phrases.notes: "He" means the second attacker, the one who finished him off.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a new ברייתא connected to the ״כל נפש״ מחלוקת from steps 3 and 4.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: From ״כל נפש אדם״: someone who kills a person who was already hit by someone else is חייב.

steps.title: If the first blow could not kill, that's obvious
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that if the first blow could not kill, of course the second attacker is חייב, so no פסוק is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: The blow could not kill? That is obvious!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the wording of the ברייתא. It says the case as written is too obvious to need a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the first blow could not kill, then the first attacker did not start a killing at all. The second attacker is simply a regular murderer. A פסוק should not be needed to teach that.

phrases.english: There is not enough force to kill? That is obvious!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the wording of the ברייתא from step 11.
steps.kashyaTarget: The case described in the ברייתא, where the first blow could not kill.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק is not used to teach something obvious. If only the second attacker really killed, his guilt needs no special source.

steps.title: Change the wording: the first blow could kill
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes the ברייתא so it talks about a first blow that was strong enough to kill, and still the second attacker is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, the ברייתא means the first blow had enough force to kill, and another person came and killed him. The second one is חייב.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers its challenge by changing the wording of the ברייתא so that it teaches something new.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now the case is a real חידוש. The victim was already dying from the first blow, which is a גוסס בידי אדם, and still the one who speeds up his death is חייב.
steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not saying there are two cases here. It replaces the case where the blow could not kill with a case where the blow could kill.

phrases.english: Rather, there is enough force to kill,
and another comes and kills him,
that he is liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge of step 12 by changing the case in the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changing the wording of the ברייתא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברייתא was about a first blow that could not kill.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about a first blow that could kill, and the one who finishes the victim is still חייב.

steps.title: This ברייתא follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא
steps.stepSummary: The unattributed ברייתא matches the view of רבי יהודה בן בתירא, who holds that the one who speeds up a death is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this unattributed ברייתא follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא identifies whose opinion the corrected ברייתא follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The רבנן say a killer is חייב only for taking a whole life. רבי יהודה בן בתירא says he is חייב even for taking a little life. A second attacker who kills someone already dying took only a little life, so he is חייב only according to רבי יהודה בן בתירא.

keyTerms.meaning: An unattributed teaching that names no specific author
Following the view of רבי יהודה בן בתירא

steps.whatToRemember: The ברייתא as corrected says that one who kills a person dying from an earlier deadly blow is חייב. This matches רבי יהודה בן בתירא's reading of ״כל נפש״ as any amount of life.

phrases.english: And this unattributed teaching is in accordance with Rabbi Yehuda ben Beteira.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Identifies whose view the corrected ברייתא of step 13 follows.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The unattributed ברייתא, which makes the final killer חייב even when an earlier blow was deadly, follows רבי יהודה בן בתירא and not the רבנן.

steps.title: Killing a טריפה, and a טריפה who kills
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that one who kills a טריפה is פטור. A טריפה who kills is חייב if it happened in front of the בית דין, and פטור if it did not.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said: Someone who kills a טריפה is exempt. A טריפה who kills someone in front of the court is liable. If it was not in front of the court, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a new ruling with two halves. One half is about killing a טריפה, and the other is about a טריפה who kills.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a טריפה is treated like someone already as good as dead, killing him is not punished as murder. A טריפה who murders can be punished, but only if the judges saw it themselves. The גמרא will explain the reason for this split right away.

keyTerms.meaning: A person with a fatal injury to a vital organ, treated as if already as good as dead
In front of the court, so the judges saw it themselves

steps.confusionAlert: פטור here means the killer is not put to death by the בית דין. It does not mean killing a טריפה is permitted.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רָבָא: הַהוֹרֵג אֶת הַטְּרֵיפָה – פָּטוּר.
phrases.english: Rava said: One who kills a tereifa is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: וּטְרֵיפָה שֶׁהָרַג בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: And a tereifa who killed in front of the court is liable;
not in front of the court, he is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבָא: הַהוֹרֵג אֶת הַטְּרֵיפָה – פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the earlier idea (step 10) that a טריפה is like someone whose vital organs are already cut, and turns it into practical rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Killing a טריפה is פטור. A טריפה who kills is חייב only if it happened in front of the בית דין.

steps.title: Why is the טריפה liable in front of the court?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the source that a טריפה who kills in front of the בית דין is חייב.
steps.simpleTranslation: In front of the court, what is the reason he is liable?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the first half of רבא's ruling about a טריפה who kills. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally a court punishes based on what witnesses say. Here the judges saw it themselves, so the גמרא wants to know what lets the court punish in this case.

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין, מַאי טַעְמָא חַיָּיב?
phrases.english: In front of the court, what is the reason he is liable?

steps.triggerLanguage: בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין, מַאי טַעְמָא חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reasoning behind רבא's ruling in step 15.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source that lets the court punish a טריפה who killed in front of the judges.

steps.title: The פסוק, and the problem of testimony that cannot face הזמה
steps.stepSummary: In front of the בית דין he is חייב because of ״ובערת הרע מקרבך״. Without the court seeing it he is פטור, because testimony against a טריפה can never be made into הזמה, and such testimony does not count.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: 'And you shall remove the evil from your midst.' Not in front of the court he is exempt, because this is testimony that you cannot make into conspiring testimony, and any testimony like that is not considered testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains both halves of רבא's rule about a טריפה who kills. One half uses a פסוק, and the other uses a rule about witnesses.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the judges see the murder themselves, the פסוק tells them to remove the evil. When only witnesses testify, there is a problem. If they were found to be עדים זוממין, they could not be put to death, because they only plotted to kill a טריפה, and killing a טריפה is פטור. Testimony that can never be punished through הזמה is not valid testimony at all.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And you shall remove the evil from your midst'
To make it into הזמה, meaning to catch the witnesses as plotting liars who get the punishment they planned

steps.whatToRemember: Testimony that can never lead to the witnesses being punished as עדים זוממין is not valid testimony. Since plotting to kill a טריפה carries no death penalty, witnesses alone cannot convict a טריפה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that testimony which cannot face הזמה is not testimony, is a basic principle of the laws of witnesses.

phrases.english: As it is written: "And you shall remove the evil from your midst."
phrases.notes: דברים 13:6

phrases.english: Not in front of the court, he is exempt,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָוְיָא לַהּ עֵדוּת שֶׁאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לַהֲזִימָּהּ,
phrases.english: because it is testimony that you cannot make into conspiring testimony,
phrases.notes: If these witnesses turned out to be liars, they could not be killed, since they only plotted against a טריפה.

phrases.aramaic: וְכׇל עֵדוּת שֶׁאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לַהֲזִימָּהּ –
phrases.english: and any testimony that you cannot make into conspiring testimony
is not called testimony.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 16 and also explains the second half of רבא's ruling.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: In front of the court, the פסוק ״ובערת הרע מקרבך״ makes him liable. Without the court seeing it, witness testimony against him cannot face הזמה, so it is not valid.

steps.title: The same rulings for forbidden relations with a male
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that one who has forbidden relations with a male טריפה is חייב. A טריפה who does this is חייב in front of the בית דין and פטור otherwise, for the same reasons as before.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: One who has relations with a male who is a טריפה is liable. A טריפה who does this in front of the court is liable; not in front of the court, he is exempt. In front of the court he is liable because of 'And you shall remove the evil from your midst.' Not in front of the court he is exempt, because it is testimony that cannot be made into conspiring testimony.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives a second ruling with the same two-part shape, this time about forbidden relations between males instead of murder.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The big change is in the first half. Killing a טריפה was פטור, but having relations with a טריפה is חייב. The second half, about a טריפה who sins, uses the same reasoning as the murder case.

keyTerms.meaning: One who has forbidden relations with a male
Had forbidden relations with a male

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הָרוֹבֵעַ אֶת הַטְּרֵיפָה – חַיָּיב.
phrases.english: And Rava said: One who has relations with a male tereifa is liable.

phrases.aramaic: טְרֵיפָה שֶׁרָבַע, בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: A tereifa who had relations with a male, in front of the court, is liable;
not in front of the court, he is exempt.

phrases.aramaic: בִּפְנֵי בֵּית דִּין חַיָּיב, דִּכְתִיב: ״וּבִעַרְתָּ הָרַע מִקִּרְבֶּךָ״.
phrases.english: In front of the court he is liable, as it is written: "And you shall remove the evil from your midst."
Not in front of the court he is exempt,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָוְיָא לַהּ עֵדוּת שֶׁאִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לַהֲזִימָּהּ.
phrases.english: because it is testimony that you cannot make into conspiring testimony.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָבָא: הָרוֹבֵעַ אֶת הַטְּרֵיפָה – חַיָּיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A parallel ruling by רבא that uses the same structure and reasons as steps 15 to 17.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: One who has relations with a male טריפה is חייב. A טריפה who does so is חייב only in front of the בית דין.

steps.title: Why say the second ruling at all?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why רבא needed the second ruling, since it seems identical to the first.
steps.simpleTranslation: Why do I need this too? It is the same as that!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבא for repeating himself, since the second ruling looks like a copy of the first.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The part about a טריפה who sins, with the פסוק and the הזמה reason, is exactly the same in both rulings. So the גמרא asks what the second ruling adds.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need this as well?
This is the same as that

phrases.english: Why do I need this too?
This is the same as that!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 18 as repeating step 15.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Its structure and reasons match the murder ruling exactly, so it seems to add nothing new.

steps.title: The new point: relations with a טריפה are still punished
steps.stepSummary: The second ruling was needed for its first half. We might have thought relations with a טריפה are like relations with a dead body and are פטור. רבא teaches that the punishment depends on pleasure, and here there is pleasure.
steps.simpleTranslation: The case of one who has relations with a טריפה was needed. You might have said: let him be like one who has relations with a dead body, and be exempt. רבא teaches us that the liability is because of pleasure, and this person does have pleasure.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the second ruling teaches something new in its first half, about someone who has relations with a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since killing a טריפה is פטור because he counts like a dead person, we might think relations with him are like relations with a dead body, which carry no death penalty. The answer is that for forbidden relations, what matters is the pleasure the sinner gets. A טריפה is truly alive, so the pleasure is real and the sinner is חייב.

keyTerms.meaning: You might have said, introducing a mistaken first thought
One who has relations with a dead body

steps.whatToRemember: A טריפה counts like a dead person when it comes to murder. For forbidden relations, though, the sin depends on pleasure, so relations with a טריפה are fully punishable.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two halves. The repeat is in the half about a טריפה who sins. The new point is in the half about someone who sins with a טריפה.
steps.whyThisMatters: It shows that the status of a טריפה as 'like dead' does not apply everywhere. It depends on what each kind of sin is about.

phrases.english: The case of one who has relations with a tereifa, he needed it.
You might have said:
Let him be like one who has relations with a dead body, and be exempt?
phrases.notes: This is the mistaken first thought, since a טריפה counts like a dead person when it comes to murder.

phrases.aramaic: קָא מַשְׁמַע לַן, דְּמִשּׁוּם הֲנָאָה הוּא,
phrases.english: It teaches us that the liability is because of pleasure,
and this one does have pleasure.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 19 by pointing to what is new in the second ruling.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Identifies the new point (צריכותא) in the half of the ruling that is not repeated.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Relations with a טריפה are like relations with a dead body and are פטור.
steps.terutzMaskana: Liability for forbidden relations depends on pleasure, and a living טריפה gives real pleasure, so the sinner is חייב.

steps.title: רבא on witnesses and a טריפה
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that witnesses who testified against a טריפה and became זוממין are not killed, but witnesses who are themselves טריפה and became זוממין are killed.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: Witnesses who testified against a טריפה and were then proven to be plotting witnesses are not killed. Witnesses who are themselves טריפה and were proven to be plotting witnesses are killed.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives two rulings about a טריפה and the law of עדים זוממין. One is about witnesses who testified against a טריפה, and the other is about witnesses who are themselves a טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טריפה is treated like a dead man, so witnesses who plotted to kill him did not plot to kill a real living person, and they are not killed. But when the witnesses themselves are טריפה, they did plot against a healthy person, so רבא says they are killed like any עדים זוממין.

keyTerms.meaning: Plotting witnesses; other witnesses prove they could not have seen what they claimed, and they get the punishment they tried to cause
They were made into זוממין (proven to be plotting witnesses)
Witnesses who are themselves a טריפה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the two cases. In the first, the person they testified AGAINST is a טריפה. In the second, the WITNESSES themselves are טריפה.

phrases.english: And רבא said:
Witnesses who testified against a טריפה
and were proven to be plotting witnesses are not killed.
Witnesses who are טריפה who were proven to be plotting witnesses are killed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds another ruling to רבא's series of טריפה rulings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Plotting against a טריפה does not bring death to the plotting witnesses. Plotting witnesses who are themselves טריפה are killed.

steps.title: רב אשי: טריפה witnesses are not killed
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי disagrees: even witnesses who are טריפה are not killed when they become זוממין, because the witnesses who prove them זוממין could never be made זוממין themselves.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even witnesses who are טריפה who were proven to be plotting witnesses are not killed. This is because they cannot be part of a case of 'plotters of plotters'.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי argues on רבא's second ruling and says that טריפה witnesses who become זוממין are not killed either.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Picture a second set of witnesses who prove the טריפה witnesses are זוממין. If this second set were later proven to be זוממין themselves, they could never be killed, because they plotted to kill a טריפה. Testimony that can never be made into הזמה does not count, so the טריפה witnesses can't be punished on its basis.

keyTerms.meaning: Plotters of plotters; the witnesses who proved the first witnesses to be זוממין, being proven זוממין themselves

steps.confusionAlert: רב אשי is not saying the טריפה witnesses did nothing wrong. He is saying the testimony that would punish them is testimony that can't be made into הזמה, so it can't be used.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ עֵדֵי טְרֵיפָה
phrases.english: רב אשי said: Even witnesses who are טריפה
who were proven to be plotting witnesses are not killed,
because they cannot be part of a case of 'plotters of plotters'.
phrases.notes: The witnesses who proved them זוממין could never be killed if they turned out to be זוממין too, since they plotted against a טריפה. This is the same idea as step 17.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ עֵדֵי טְרֵיפָה שֶׁהוּזַּמּוּ אֵין נֶהֱרָגִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the second half of רבא's ruling in step 21.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Witnesses who are טריפה and become זוממין are not killed, because the testimony against them could never itself be made into הזמה.

steps.title: רבא on an ox that kills
steps.stepSummary: רבא rules that an ox that is a טריפה and kills is liable to be stoned, but an ox whose owner is a טריפה is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבא said: An ox that is a טריפה and killed a person is liable. An ox that belongs to a person who is a טריפה and killed a person is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives another טריפה ruling, this time about an ox that kills a person. He contrasts an ox that is itself טריפה with an ox whose owner is טריפה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally an ox that kills a person is stoned. רבא says the ox being a טריפה does not save it, but the owner being a טריפה does. The גמרא will explain why next.

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמַר רָבָא: שׁוֹר טְרֵיפָה שֶׁהָרַג – חַיָּיב,
phrases.english: And רבא said: An ox that is a טריפה that killed is liable,
and the ox of a person who is a טריפה
that killed is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Another ruling in רבא's series about טריפה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טריפה ox that kills is stoned. An ox of a טריפה owner that kills is exempt.

steps.title: Why is the ox of a טריפה exempt?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks for the reason behind רבא's ruling.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks why רבא ruled this way. This short question sets up the answer that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The puzzle is mainly the second half of the ruling. Why should the owner's status matter at all when it is the ox that killed?

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the source of רבא's ruling in step 23.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The source showing that the owner's status as a טריפה exempts his ox.

steps.title: The verse links the ox to its owner
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק puts the ox's stoning and the owner's death together, so the ox is stoned only where the owner could be put to death.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'The ox shall be stoned and its owner also shall be put to death.' Wherever 'and its owner also shall be put to death' can apply, 'the ox shall be stoned' applies. Wherever 'and its owner also shall be put to death' cannot apply, 'the ox shall be stoned' does not apply.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a פסוק that mentions the ox and its owner in the same breath. It learns that the two go together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A טריפה owner cannot normally be put to death: testimony against a טריפה can never face הזמה, so it is not valid testimony (step 17). So the second half of the פסוק can't apply to him, and therefore the first half (stoning his ox) can't apply either. When the ox itself is טריפה, the owner is healthy, so the ox is still stoned.

keyTerms.meaning: We read about it; the פסוק applies to it

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the ox's punishment depends on the owner being someone who could be punished. רב אשי will use the same link between ox and owner in a different way.

phrases.english: The verse says:
'The ox shall be stoned and its owner also shall be put to death.'
phrases.notes: שמות 21:29

phrases.aramaic: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּקָרֵינָא בֵּיהּ ״וְגַם בְּעָלָיו יוּמָת״,
phrases.english: Wherever we can read about it 'and its owner also shall be put to death,'
we read about it 'the ox shall be stoned,'

phrases.aramaic: וְכֹל הֵיכָא דְּלָא קָרֵינַן בֵּיהּ ״וְגַם בְּעָלָיו יוּמָת״,
phrases.english: and wherever we cannot read about it 'and its owner also shall be put to death,'
phrases.notes: An owner who is a טריפה can't be put to death through witnesses, because testimony against a טריפה can't face הזמה (step 17).

phrases.english: we do not read about it 'the ox shall be stoned.'

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר קְרָא: הַשּׁוֹר יִסָּקֵל וְגַם בְּעָלָיו יוּמָת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 24.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק links the ox's stoning to the owner's being put to death. Where the owner can't be killed (a טריפה), the ox isn't stoned.

steps.title: רב אשי: even a טריפה ox is exempt
steps.stepSummary: רב אשי disagrees with רבא and says that even an ox that is itself a טריפה is exempt when it kills.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אשי said: Even an ox that is a טריפה that killed is also exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אשי argues on the first half of רבא's ruling. He holds that a טריפה ox that kills is not stoned.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא said a טריפה ox is liable. רב אשי says it is exempt, so now both kinds of ox in רבא's ruling come out exempt. His reason comes next.

phrases.aramaic: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ שׁוֹר טְרֵיפָה נָמֵי
phrases.english: רב אשי said: Even an ox that is a טריפה also
that killed is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: רַב אָשֵׁי אָמַר: אֲפִילּוּ שׁוֹר טְרֵיפָה נָמֵי שֶׁהָרַג
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Disagrees with the first half of רבא's ruling in step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A טריפה ox that kills is exempt from stoning.

steps.title: רב אשי's reason: the ox is like its owner
steps.stepSummary: Since an owner who is a טריפה would be exempt, an ox that is a טריפה is also exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason? Since if the owner were a טריפה he would be exempt, an ox that is a טריפה is also exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for רב אשי's reason and answers it right away. A טריפה ox is treated just like a טריפה owner.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב אשי also uses the link between ox and owner from the פסוק, but he takes it further. Whatever exempts the owner, here being a טריפה, also exempts the ox when the ox is in that same condition.
steps.whatToRemember: רבא: a טריפה ox is stoned, but an ox of a טריפה owner is not. רב אשי: both are exempt, because the ox follows the same rule as the owner.

phrases.english: What is the reason?
Since if the owner were a טריפה he would be exempt,
phrases.notes: The words 'a טריפה' are not written here, but the גמרא assumes them.

phrases.english: an ox that is a טריפה is also exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא? כֵּיוָן דְּאִילּוּ בְּעָלִים הֲווֹ פְּטִירִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason for רב אשי's ruling in step 26.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The ox is compared to its owner. A טריפה owner is exempt, so a טריפה ox is exempt too.

steps.title: Back to the משנה: setting a dog on someone
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה about setting a dog or snake on someone, to begin discussing it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'If he set the dog on him, etc.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new topic by quoting the opening words of a line in the משנה. This step sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says that someone who sets a dog or snake on a person is exempt. It also says that if he pressed the snake's fangs into the person, רבי יהודה holds him liable while the חכמים exempt him. The גמרא is about to explain רבי יהודה's view.

keyTerms.meaning: Etc.; the quote of the משנה continues

phrases.english: If he set the dog on him, etc.
phrases.notes: This is a quote from our משנה. The 'etc.' points to the rest of it, including the case of pressing a snake's fangs into someone.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the טריפה rulings and goes back to the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who sets a dog or snake on a person is exempt. In the case of pressing in the snake's fangs, רבי יהודה holds him liable and the חכמים exempt him.

steps.title: For רבי יהודה, the venom is already in the snake's teeth
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב explains that רבי יהודה holds the snake's venom sits ready between its teeth, so the snake does nothing active.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב אחא בר יעקב said: When you look into it, you will find that according to רבי יהודה, a snake's venom sits between its teeth.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב explains the thinking behind רבי יהודה's view in the משנה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the venom is already sitting in the teeth, the snake doesn't have to do anything for the bite to kill. So the person who presses the fangs into the victim did the whole killing himself.

keyTerms.meaning: When you look into it, you will find

phrases.english: רב אחא בר יעקב said:
When you look into it, you will find,
according to רבי יהודה,

phrases.aramaic: אֶרֶס נָחָשׁ בֵּין שִׁינָּיו הוּא עוֹמֵד.
phrases.english: a snake's venom sits between its teeth.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב אַחָא בַּר יַעֲקֹב: כְּשֶׁתִּמְצָא לוֹמַר לְדִבְרֵי רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reasoning of רבי יהודה in the משנה quoted in step 28.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יהודה, the snake's venom is already in its teeth, so the snake is passive.

steps.title: The one who presses the fangs is killed, the snake is exempt
steps.stepSummary: So the person who made the snake bite is killed by the sword like a murderer, and the snake is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, the one who makes the snake bite is killed by the sword, and the snake is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב draws the result of his explanation. The person is the killer, and the snake is not punished.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the snake did nothing active, the person is treated as a murderer, and a murderer is killed by the sword. The snake is like a tool in his hand, so it is not stoned the way an animal that kills is.

keyTerms.meaning: The sword; the death penalty given to a murderer

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבי יהודה, pressing a snake's fangs into someone is direct murder. The person is killed by the sword, and the snake is exempt.

phrases.english: Therefore, the one who makes it bite is killed by the sword,
and the snake is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the practical result of רב אחא בר יעקב's explanation in step 29.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to רבי יהודה, the one who presses the snake's fangs in is killed by the sword, and the snake is exempt.

steps.title: The חכמים' view: the snake releases its own venom
steps.stepSummary: רב אחא בר יעקב continues. According to the חכמים, a snake releases its venom on its own.
steps.simpleTranslation: According to the חכמים, a snake brings out its venom by itself.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב continues and gives the other side of the snake case. He explains how the חכמים understand the way a snake's bite works.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה held that the venom just sits ready between the snake's teeth, so the snake does nothing active. The חכמים disagree. They hold that the snake itself actively pushes out the venom. That makes the snake the one who really does the killing.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages (the majority opinion against רבי יהודה)

phrases.english: According to the words of the Sages,
a snake's venom, it discharges by itself.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the חכמים's reasoning, parallel to רבי יהודה's reasoning in step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, the snake actively releases its own venom.

steps.title: So the snake is stoned and the person is exempt
steps.stepSummary: Because the snake does the act itself, the snake is stoned and the one who made it bite is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore the snake is put to death by stoning, and the person who made it bite is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: רב אחא בר יעקב draws the practical result from the חכמים's reasoning. The snake gets the death penalty, and the person goes free from execution.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the snake itself released the venom, the snake is the real killer. So it is stoned, like an animal that kills. The person only set things in motion, so the court does not execute him. This is the exact reverse of רבי יהודה's result in step 30.

keyTerms.meaning: Stoning, the death penalty for an animal that kills
The one who causes the snake to bite

steps.whatToRemember: The whole argument depends on one question: who actually releases the venom? For רבי יהודה it is the person, so the person is killed by the sword. For the חכמים it is the snake, so the snake is stoned and the person is exempt.
steps.confusionAlert: "Exempt" here means the court does not execute him. It does not mean he did nothing wrong.

phrases.english: Therefore: the snake is stoned,
and the one who made it bite is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the halachic result from step 31's reasoning.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: According to the חכמים, the snake is stoned and the person who made it bite is exempt from execution.

steps.title: New משנה: victim improved, then got worse and died
steps.stepSummary: Someone strikes another person, and the doctors expect him to die. He improves, then worsens and dies. The תנא קמא says the attacker is liable. רבי נחמיה says he is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: If someone hits another person with a stone or a fist, and the doctors estimate he will die, but he gets better and later gets worse and dies, the attacker is liable. רבי נחמיה says he is exempt, because there is a reason to think something else killed him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with a new case about someone who struck a blow and the victim later died. Two opinions disagree about whether the attacker is liable.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תנא קמא blames the original blow for the death, even though the victim improved for a while. רבי נחמיה says the improvement gives a real basis to think the death came from something else. So he holds the attacker cannot be executed.

keyTerms.meaning: They assessed him as going to die
There is a basis for the matter (a reason to think so)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the whole next discussion. How sure must we be that the blow caused the death before we execute a killer?

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who strikes his fellow,
whether with a stone or with a fist,
and they assessed him as going to die,
phrases.notes: "They" are the experts who judge how bad the injury is.

phrases.english: and he got better than he had been,
and afterward he got worse and died — he is liable.
Rabbi Neḥemya says: he is exempt,
since there is a basis for the matter.
phrases.notes: Literally "there are legs to the matter." He means the improvement gives good reason to think the blow did not kill him.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַמַּכֶּה אֶת חֲבֵירוֹ, בֵּין בְּאֶבֶן בֵּין בְּאֶגְרוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה, unrelated to the snake discussion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The תנא קמא holds the attacker liable even though the victim improved before dying. רבי נחמיה exempts him.

steps.title: ברייתא: the פסוק רבי נחמיה expounded
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that רבי נחמיה learned his ruling from a פסוק, and begins quoting it.
steps.simpleTranslation: The רבנן taught: רבי נחמיה expounded this: "If he rises and walks outside..."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts its discussion of the משנה by bringing a ברייתא about where רבי נחמיה got his opinion. This is a setup line, and the פסוק and the derivation continue right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי נחמיה's ruling is not just a common-sense guess. The ברייתא connects it to the פסוק about a victim who gets up and walks outside. The גמרא is preparing to show how that פסוק supports exempting the attacker.

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
This is what Rabbi Neḥemya expounded,
"If he rises and walks outside
phrases.notes: שמות 21:19. The quote keeps going in the next lines of the גמרא.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: אֶת זוֹ דָּרַשׁ רַבִּי נְחֶמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא on the משנה by bringing the source for רבי נחמיה's opinion.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי נחמיה's exemption comes from expounding the פסוק "אם יקום והתהלך בחוץ".
